messages:
noah: Hey all, hitting a weird blocker on my company MacBook Pro (Monterey 12.6). MDM enrollment completed but my dev tooling (Homebrew + a Docker helper kext) fails to load with: "System Extension Blocked". The Security & Privacy pane asks for admin approval but I don't have the admin prompt when I click "Allow". Any ideas?

it_bot: IT ticket created: #IT-4668. Please include a photo/screenshot of the System Preferences prompt and output of `spctl kext-consent list` and `profiles status -type enrollment`.

claire_it: hi @noah 0: welcome! For corporate-owned macs we allow dev kernel extensions only after an admin vetting step. Two quick things: 1) did you enroll using the corporate Wi-Fi (not home VPN) during enrollment? 2) can you paste `profiles -P | grep -i kext -A2`?

noah: enrolled on office wifi. screenshot attached. Here's `spctl` output:
```
$ spctl kext-consent list
TeamIdentifiers: NONE
```
And `profiles status -type enrollment` shows Enrolled: Yes.

claire_it: thanks. That TeamIdentifiers: NONE is fine. The missing piece is that the kext's developer team ID needs to be pre-approved by our endpoint policy. Opened a request to the security admin to add the TeamID shown in your helper's installer. @sam_admin can you check pending system extension approvals?

sam_admin: I see a pending System Extension Allow request for noah's serial (C02Z12345XYZ). Approving now, giving explicit consent for TeamID T24ABCD9EF. Also pushed a local sudo-approved plist to the device.

mike_devx: for future, we prefer moving away from kexts -> the helper has a userland alternative. I'll DM @noah a brew formula for the userland variant that doesn't require System Extension approval.

it_bot: IT ticket #IT-4668 updated: system extension approval granted by sam_admin.

noah: tried rebooting after the approval and plugin loaded. Docker helper now starts, and my dev containers come up. Thanks!

noah: one small note 0: when clicking Allow in Security & Privacy, Safari didn't surface the prompt. Switching to Chrome did show the Allow button. Might be a macOS quirk worth documenting.

claire_it: good catch. We'll add a line in the onboarding checklist: "If Security & Privacy Allow doesn't appear in Safari, try Chrome/Edge and then reboot. Contact IT with serial and screenshot if still blocked."

it_bot: Ticket #IT-4668 marked resolved by sam_admin.

noah: thanks team! All set, leaving a quick onboarding tip in the new-hires doc. Appreciate the fast turnaround. :tada:
